notes.WRSPM: Phenomena (individuals, events, states) with environment- vs machine-controlled partition and shared phenomena give the 2s (domain_entity, event, interaction); W (domain assumptions) is first-class domain_property; R (requirements) is treated as a partial goal, and the environment/machine split as partial actor and context.
notes.Problem Frames: Problem domains with types (causal, biddable, lexical, machine), domain descriptions, shared-phenomena interfaces, the context diagram and event phenomena are first-class; requirement (dashed oval) is only a partial goal, and the constrains relation and operations are partial constraint/action.
notes.KAOS: Goal, Agent, Object (entity/association/event) and Operation models plus domain properties and formal temporal-logic assertions (Achieve/Maintain, bounded operators) and monitor/control/context-diagram links give the 2s; obstacles (uncertainty), goal categories/soft goals (quality), constraints and resources (1993 meta-model), scenarios/state machines and goal Source attribute are partial.
notes.iStar: Actor (agent/role/position), Goal, Quality (softgoal), Task, Resource and Dependency link are first-class; actors double as stakeholders without a distinct construct and Resource is the only domain-entity-like element; no context, time, event or provenance constructs.
notes.CORE: Participant (stakeholder), Goal, Softgoal, Quality constraint and Domain assumption are the first-class elements; Plan gives partial action, participants' communicated information/attitudes give partial provenance, and participants give partial actor.
notes.Dey: Context definition with entity (person, place, object) and primary context types identity/location/time/activity: context, time, location and domain_entity are first-class; identity/user gives partial actor, status as entity attribute partial domain_property, activity partial action.
notes.Contextual goal models: Context (activation/applicability conditions on goals and tasks) and Tropos-style Actor, Goal and Task constructs are first-class; softgoals, domain assumptions/world facts, dependencies and context-driven variability are partial or secondary.
notes.Uncertainty taxonomy: Taxonomy of uncertainty (sources, level, nature, emergence, location in model) makes uncertainty first-class; environment/context as a source, emergence phase as a temporal attribute and assumptions are partial; it models no system entities or behaviour.
notes.RELAX: Uncertainty is explicit through ENV/MON/REL/DEP and relaxation of SHALL requirements; temporal operators (EVENTUALLY, BEFORE, AFTER, UNTIL, IN) are first-class time; ENV gives environment properties (domain_property 2), with partial entity, context, interaction, event and goal links.
notes.ISO 29148: Stakeholder requirements/StRS, requirement types (quality/performance/usability, interface, design constraints) are named constructs giving the 2s; ConOps/operational scenarios, assumptions, TBD handling, rationale/source/traceability attributes, timing and functional requirements are textual or attribute-level 1s.
notes.SysML v2: Requirement def/usage with actor and stakeholder parameters, constraint def/usage (require/assume), part/item/attribute definitions, action, state, event occurrence, connection/interface/flow and satisfy/verify/derive relationships are first-class; goal/objective, quality-via-attributes, time slices, spatial items and assume-context are partial.
notes.Traceability reference model: Stakeholder/source objects and the trace link types (rationale, satisfaction, evolution, allocation) make stakeholder and provenance first-class; requirement dependency links give partial interaction; the model carries no domain, behaviour or quality constructs.
